plan.chapterName: OpenStax University Physics, chapter 33: Electromagnetic Waves
plan.contextChunk: This figure places two three-dimensional electromagnetic wave diagrams side by side along one horizontal propagation line that ends at the right in a green arrowhead labeled c. In each, the electric field is a red sinusoid oscillating in the vertical plane, filled with a comb of short arrows running from the axis up to the curve, while the magnetic field is a matching blue sinusoid in the horizontal plane, drawn in perspective as flattened lobes with arrows of its own. Pale teal square panels stand upright along the axis so the two perpendicular oscillation planes stay legible. The left wave is the smaller; black leaders at its left end label the red curve E and the blue curve B, and the symbol u sits above it. The right wave carries visibly taller red lobes and wider blue lobes over the same wavelength, its leaders read 2E and 2B, and the label above it is 4u. Drawing both on a single axis at identical wavelength isolates amplitude as the only difference, so the paired labels above carry the comparison. The figure introduces amplitude as what governs the energy an electromagnetic wave stores and transports.

elements: Single straight black propagation axis running left-to-right through both wave groups (the common x-axis)
Green arrowhead terminating the axis at the far right, labeled 'c'
Left wave: red sinusoid oscillating in the vertical (x-y) plane, amplitude E, about two wavelengths long
Left wave: comb of short red arrows drawn from the axis up (and down) to the red curve at regular x-intervals, arrowheads on the curve
Left wave: blue sinusoid oscillating in the horizontal (x-z) plane, amplitude B, drawn in perspective as flattened lobes, same wavelength and phase as the red curve
Left wave: comb of short blue arrows from the axis out to the blue curve, arrowheads on the curve
Left wave: two pale teal upright square panels standing perpendicular to the axis, marking the vertical oscillation plane
Right wave: red sinusoid of amplitude 2E with taller comb arrows, same wavelength as left
Right wave: blue sinusoid of amplitude 2B with wider lobes and its own arrow comb
Right wave: two pale teal upright square panels
Black leader lines with arrowheads at the left end of the left wave, labeling the red curve 'E' (vector) and the blue curve 'B' (vector)
Black leader lines at the left end of the right wave, labeling '2E' (vector) and '2B' (vector)
Text label 'u' above the left wave group
Text label '4u' above the right wave group
Faded/greyed portions of the curves where they pass behind the teal panels (depth cueing)

interactions.teaches: Energy density grows as the square of the field amplitude: doubling both E and B quadruples u, which is why the right-hand wave is labeled 4u while its wavelength is unchanged.
interactions.label: Field amplitude (× E, B)

interactions.teaches: The E and B oscillations stay perpendicular to each other and to the axis while the whole pattern travels along c, so energy is transported forward even though the fields only oscillate transversely.
interactions.label: Propagate wave along c

interactions.teaches: Switching from the field picture to the shaded energy-density picture shows that the taller/wider wave carries four times the energy per unit volume at the same wavelength.
interactions.label: View

interactions.teaches: Rotating the scene confirms the red sinusoid lies in the vertical plane and the blue in the horizontal plane — they are genuinely perpendicular, not just drawn offset.

demo_steps.title: Baseline wave, energy density u
demo_steps.narration: A single electromagnetic wave: red E oscillates vertically, blue B horizontally, both in phase along the propagation axis. Its energy density is labeled u.

demo_steps.title: Double the amplitude
demo_steps.narration: Drag the amplitude to 2. The red lobes grow taller and the blue lobes wider, but the wavelength never changes — amplitude is the only difference between the two waves in the figure.

demo_steps.title: Energy view: 4u
demo_steps.narration: Switch to the energy view. The shaded panels darken as the square of the amplitude, so 2E and 2B give 4u — four times the stored and transported energy.

demo_steps.title: Energy travels with c
demo_steps.narration: Play the animation: the transverse E and B oscillations advance together toward the green c arrow, carrying that energy flux in the propagation direction.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: World space: propagation axis is +X (screen-right), E oscillates along +Y (screen-up), B oscillates along +Z (receding diagonal). Axis is a thin black line from x = -10 to x = +10.2, ending in a green (#7FAE1B) cone arrowhead at x = +10.2 with the italic label 'c' just below-right of the tip. LEFT wave group occupies x = -10 to -2 (two full wavelengths, wavelength λ = 4 world units); RIGHT wave group occupies x = +1.5 to +9.5 (same λ = 4). Left wave: E amplitude 1.4 in +Y, B amplitude 1.4 in +Z; right wave: E amplitude 2.8, B amplitude 2.8 (exactly 2×). Both curves are E(x)=A·sin(kx), B(x)=A·sin(kx), same phase, k = 2π/4. Field-arrow combs: ~12 arrows per wavelength, each a thin shaft from the axis point (x,0,0) to the curve point, with a small cone head at the curve; red #C0392B for E, blue #1B6CA8 for B, arrow shafts slightly lighter than the curve stroke. Curve strokes ~2.5 px, red #B03030, blue #16639E. Teal panels: pale cyan squares (#A8D4D8, opacity ~0.35, faint darker border) standing upright in the Y–Z-normal sense — each panel is parallel to the X–Y screen plane? No: each panel is a square lying in the plane containing the axis and +Y (i.e. spanning X and Y) but rendered translucent; place two per wave group, spanning ~4 units in X by ~4 units in Y, centered on the axis, at x ≈ -9 and x ≈ -4 for the left wave and x ≈ +2.5 and x ≈ +7 for the right wave, each offset slightly in +Z so the blue lobes pass in front of and behind them. Portions of curves behind a panel render at ~45% opacity (grey-pink) for depth. Labels: italic 'u' in black above the left group at roughly (x=-6, y=+3.4); italic '4u' above the right group at (x=+5.5, y=+3.4). Leader lines: two black arrows from a label block at the far left ( x ≈ -12 ) pointing to the first red crest region (label 'E⃗') and to the first blue lobe (label 'B⃗'); similarly two black leaders at x ≈ -0.5 pointing right into the second group's red and blue curves, labeled '2E⃗' and '2B⃗'. Energy view: replace arrow combs with translucent filled sheets between axis and curve whose shading opacity ∝ amplitude² (u = ε0E² = ε0E0²sin²(kx); total u_right = 4·u_left), tint red→orange for electric share and blue→purple for magnetic share.
interactionPlan.notes: Build each sinusoid as a THREE.Line from a sampled CatmullRom/explicit point array (120 samples per group) so the amplitude slider can rewrite the y or z component in place. Arrow combs: instance thin CylinderGeometry shafts + ConeGeometry heads, or use ArrowHelper per sample and just update length/direction on slider change — keep count fixed to avoid rebuilds. Panels: PlaneGeometry with MeshBasicMaterial, transparent, depthWrite false, side: DoubleSide, renderOrder set so curves draw over them; use a slight opacity multiplier for the 'behind panel' segments rather than real occlusion. Labels (u, 4u, c, E, B, 2E, 2B) as CSS2DRenderer HTML overlays with leader lines drawn as separate THREE.Line segments in world space so they track under orbit. Animation: advance a phase offset φ in E(x)=A·sin(kx-φ) at constant rate; the arrow combs must be recomputed each frame (cheap at ~48 arrows total per group). Camera: standard isometric-ish pose looking slightly down from above-left so +Z recedes to lower-left, matching the source's flattened blue lobes; keep orbit damped and clamp polar angle to avoid flipping the diagram. Toggle swaps arrow-comb group visibility for filled-sheet meshes (ShapeGeometry/ribbon between axis and curve) with opacity = 0.25·(A/A0)² clamped, and updates the u / 4u label text to the live computed ratio.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Slider for field amplitude: the learner drags amplitude from E,B to 2E,2B, the red and blue wave heights grow while the energy-density label changes quadratically, showing why doubling both fields produces four times the energy density.
- Animation for propagation: the learner plays the wave moving along the c arrow, the perpendicular E and B oscillations advance together, clarifying that electromagnetic energy flux travels in the propagation direction while the fields remain transverse.
- Toggle between field view and energy view: the learner switches from the E/B wave diagram to shaded energy-density panels, making the relationship between field amplitude and transported energy visible without changing wavelength.

authoredContext:
Clearly, the larger the strength of the electric and magnetic fields, the more work they can do and the greater the energy the electromagnetic wave carries. In electromagnetic waves, the amplitude is the maximum field strength of the electric and magnetic fields (the figure). The wave energy is determined by the wave amplitude.

Energy carried by a wave depends on its amplitude. With electromagnetic waves, doubling the E fields and B fields quadruples the energy density u and the energy flux uc.

Figure on the left shows an electromagnetic wave with electric field E and magnetic field B. It is labeled u. Figure on the right shows an electromagnetic wave with electric field 2E and magnetic field 2B. Here, the amplitudes of the sine waves are doubled. The wave is labeled 4u.

Amplitude & energy of an EM wave
View
Guided demo
Drag to orbit: the red curve stays in the vertical plane, the blue one in the horizontal plane — they are genuinely perpendicular.
⚠ Figure failed to load

discrepancies: Camera/axis inclination differs: in the source the propagation axis runs nearly horizontally (slight ~8° downward tilt) across the page, whereas the generated view tilts the axis ~25–30° down to the right, making the arrangement look more aerial and compressing the horizontal B lobes.

Framing: the whole scene is rendered small and pushed into the left-centre of the canvas, leaving a large empty region, so the two wave groups read much smaller than the source's page-filling composition.

The teal reference planes are noticeably smaller relative to the waves than in the source, where the panels are large squares that extend well beyond the wave crests and clearly bracket each wave group.

The blue B sinusoid/ellipse in the horizontal plane is much less prominent than in the source (thin, flattened arrow comb) — in the original the blue lobes are broad ellipses of comparable visual weight to the red ones.
Vector labels (E⃗, B⃗, 2E⃗, 2B⃗) render the over-arrow as a faint tick and are small; the source uses bold, clearly arrowed vector symbols as the primary annotations.
evaluation.notes: Composition, two-group amplitude comparison, colors and all key labels (E, B, 2E, 2B, u, 4u, c) are faithfully reproduced with genuinely 3D perpendicular E/B combs and a rich, conceptually correct interaction set (amplitude slider, energy-density view, propagation animation, guided steps); main weaknesses are a steeper-than-source camera tilt, small framing within the canvas, and under-weighted blue B lobes/teal panels.

feedback.rationale: The concept and interaction structure are correct; remaining issues are purely rendering details—camera tilt, canvas framing/scale, plane and B-lobe visual weight, and vector label styling—which are generator-level fixes.

interactions.teaches: Energy density grows as the square of the field amplitude: doubling both E and B quadruples u, which is why the right-hand wave is labeled 4u while its wavelength is unchanged.

demo_steps.title: Baseline wave, energy density u
demo_steps.narration: A single electromagnetic wave: red E oscillates vertically, blue B horizontally, both in phase along the propagation axis. Its energy density is labeled u.

demo_steps.title: Double the amplitude
demo_steps.narration: Drag the amplitude to 2. The red lobes grow taller and the blue lobes wider, but the wavelength never changes — amplitude is the only difference between the two waves in the figure.

demo_steps.title: Energy view: 4u
demo_steps.narration: Switch to the energy view. The shaded panels darken as the square of the amplitude, so 2E and 2B give 4u — four times the stored and transported energy.

demo_steps.title: Energy travels with c
demo_steps.narration: Play the animation: the transverse E and B oscillations advance together toward the green c arrow, carrying that energy flux in the propagation direction.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: World space: propagation axis is +X (screen-right), E oscillates along +Y (screen-up), B oscillates along +Z (receding diagonal). Axis is a thin black line from x = -10 to x = +10.2, ending in a green (#7FAE1B) cone arrowhead at x = +10.2 with the italic label 'c' just below-right of the tip. LEFT wave group occupies x = -10 to -2 (two full wavelengths, wavelength λ = 4 world units); RIGHT wave group occupies x = +1.5 to +9.5 (same λ = 4). Left wave: E amplitude 1.4 in +Y, B amplitude 1.4 in +Z; right wave: E amplitude 2.8, B amplitude 2.8 (exactly 2×). Both curves are E(x)=A·sin(kx), B(x)=A·sin(kx), same phase, k = 2π/4. Field-arrow combs: ~12 arrows per wavelength, each a thin shaft from the axis point (x,0,0) to the curve point, with a small cone head at the curve; red #C0392B for E, blue #1B6CA8 for B, arrow shafts slightly lighter than the curve stroke. Curve strokes ~2.5 px, red #B03030, blue #16639E. Teal panels: pale cyan squares (#A8D4D8, opacity ~0.35, faint darker border) standing upright in the Y–Z-normal sense — each panel is parallel to the X–Y screen plane? No: each panel is a square lying in the plane containing the axis and +Y (i.e. spanning X and Y) but rendered translucent; place two per wave group, spanning ~4 units in X by ~4 units in Y, centered on the axis, at x ≈ -9 and x ≈ -4 for the left wave and x ≈ +2.5 and x ≈ +7 for the right wave, each offset slightly in +Z so the blue lobes pass in front of and behind them. Portions of curves behind a panel render at ~45% opacity (grey-pink) for depth. Labels: italic 'u' in black above the left group at roughly (x=-6, y=+3.4); italic '4u' above the right group at (x=+5.5, y=+3.4). Leader lines: two black arrows from a label block at the far left ( x ≈ -12 ) pointing to the first red crest region (label 'E⃗') and to the first blue lobe (label 'B⃗'); similarly two black leaders at x ≈ -0.5 pointing right into the second group's red and blue curves, labeled '2E⃗' and '2B⃗'. Energy view: replace arrow combs with translucent filled sheets between axis and curve whose shading opacity ∝ amplitude² (u = ε0E² = ε0E0²sin²(kx); total u_right = 4·u_left), tint red→orange for electric share and blue→purple for magnetic share.

Leader lines for E⃗/B⃗ in the source attach to the very first crest/lobe with short curved leaders; here they are long straight diagonals starting far off to the left, adding clutter.

Slim down the green c arrowhead and keep it in line with the black axis so it reads as a continuation arrow rather than a solid wedge.
Shorten and reposition the E⃗/B⃗ and 2E⃗/2B⃗ leader lines so they point to the nearest crest/lobe from just outside the wave, reducing long diagonal clutter.
